hook: Herbert Simon entered the University of Chicago in 1933 hoping to become what he called a mathematical social scientist, studying under mentors including the logician Rudolf Carnap and political scientist Charles Merriam. After finishing his undergraduate degree in 1936 and later a PhD, he built a career studying how organizations and individuals actually make decisions under limits of time, knowledge and computing power, a theory he called bounded rationality. In 1949 he joined the Carnegie Institute of Technology, now Carnegie Mellon University, to help build its Graduate School of Industrial Administration around economics and behavioral science. Around 1954 he began working with Allen Newell to use computer simulation to study human problem solving, and together with Cliff Shaw they built the Logic Theorist in 1956, widely considered the first program designed to mimic human reasoning, followed by the more general General Problem Solver in 1957. Simon spent the rest of his career at Carnegie Mellon studying cognition, organizations and artificial intelligence, work recognized with the 1975 ACM Turing Award, shared with Newell, and the 1978 Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences for his research on decision making in economic organizations.
name: Herbert Simon

quote.text: A wealth of information creates a poverty of attention.
quote.context: From Herbert Simon's essay Designing Organizations for an Information-Rich World, 1971

moniker: Nobel laureate who founded artificial intelligence alongside Allen Newell

timeline.event: Born in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, to a German immigrant electrical engineer and an American-born pianist
timeline.impact: Grew up in a household that valued both technical and intellectual pursuits

timeline.event: Completes his undergraduate degree at the University of Chicago
timeline.impact: Studied under mentors in economics, logic and political science, shaping his lifelong interest in decision making

timeline.event: Joins the Carnegie Institute of Technology to help establish its Graduate School of Industrial Administration
timeline.impact: Grounded a new business school in economics and behavioral science rather than traditional management theory

timeline.event: Builds the Logic Theorist with Allen Newell and Cliff Shaw
timeline.impact: Demonstrated that a machine could carry out steps resembling human logical reasoning, a foundational moment for artificial intelligence

timeline.event: Develops the General Problem Solver with Allen Newell
timeline.impact: Extended machine problem solving toward a more general model of human reasoning strategies

timeline.event: Receives the ACM A.M. Turing Award jointly with Allen Newell
timeline.impact: Recognized their joint contributions to artificial intelligence and the psychology of human cognition

timeline.event: Awarded the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences
timeline.impact: Honored his research on how real organizations make decisions under limited information, known as bounded rationality

timeline.event: Dies in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, on February 9
timeline.impact: Leaves a body of work spanning economics, psychology, computer science and artificial intelligence

quick_facts: Joined Carnegie Institute of Technology, now Carnegie Mellon University, in 1949
Built the Logic Theorist with Allen Newell and Cliff Shaw in 1956, an early program designed to prove mathematical theorems the way a person might
Developed the General Problem Solver with Newell in 1957 to model general human problem solving
Won the ACM Turing Award in 1975 jointly with Allen Newell
Won the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences in 1978 for research on decision making inside economic organizations
Introduced the concept of bounded rationality to describe how real decision makers reason under limited time and information

achievements.title: Logic Theorist, 1956
achievements.impact: Built with Allen Newell and Cliff Shaw, it is widely regarded as one of the first programs built to simulate human problem solving and helped establish artificial intelligence as a research field.

achievements.title: General Problem Solver, 1957
achievements.impact: Extended the ideas behind the Logic Theorist into a more general program intended to model human problem solving strategies across different kinds of tasks.

achievements.title: Bounded rationality
achievements.impact: Reframed economic and organizational decision theory around the practical limits of human information and computation, reshaping economics, management science and later behavioral economics.

achievements.title: ACM A.M. Turing Award, 1975
achievements.impact: Shared with Allen Newell for their contributions to artificial intelligence and the psychology of human cognition.

achievements.title: Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences, 1978
achievements.impact: Awarded for his pioneering research into the decision making process within economic organizations.
